description: Reviewed, time-boxed npm-audit exceptions, enforced by scripts/check-audit-allowlist.mjs from ci.yml. Procedure: open a normal PR adding an entry below with the advisory's numeric id (the `source` field from `npm audit --json`), the affected package, a reason it can't be fixed immediately, your GitHub username as approvedBy, today's date as addedOn, and expiresOn no more than ~30 days out. A maintainer reviews and merges that PR like any other change -- the exception is recorded in git history, not typed into a runner console under time pressure. Once expiresOn passes, the exception silently stops applying and the advisory blocks CI again until it is renewed (with a fresh justification) or fixed for real. Remove the entry the moment a real fix lands -- this file is a documented escalation valve, not a place to bury advisories indefinitely.
port: Ported from mcp-tool-shop-org/merchant-league (scripts/check-audit-allowlist.mjs, its test and this file, merchant-league ed872e53), itself ported from mcp-tool-shop-org/brand. It reads `npm audit --json` from site/. Each entry needs `range`, the advisory's vulnerable range as npm reports it (whitespace is ignored). An entry stops applying at expiresOn, or as soon as the reported range differs from `range`, or npm reports a fix for the package, whichever comes first.

exceptions.reason: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (ReDoS through repeated extglobs, high): every version <= 4.0.7 is affected and no patched release exists yet. picomatch reaches this repo only through the static-site build toolchain (astro, via vite and tinyglobby); exploiting it needs an attacker-supplied glob pattern, and every glob in our site config is our own. The site ships static HTML, and the Python package has no dependencies, so nothing a lane installs uses picomatch. Remove this entry in the PR that bumps to a patched picomatch.
